class TestComputeSignalOverlap:
    """Tests for compute_signal_overlap (Jaccard similarity on signal IDs)."""

    def test_both_empty_returns_zero(self):
        """Both empty sets should yield 0.0."""
        result = compute_signal_overlap([], [])
        assert result == 0.0, f"Expected 0.0 for two empty sets, got {result}"

    def test_identical_sets_returns_one(self):
        """Identical non-empty sets should yield 1.0."""
        signals = ["s1", "s2", "s3"]
        result = compute_signal_overlap(signals, signals)
        assert result == 1.0, f"Expected 1.0 for identical sets, got {result}"

    def test_disjoint_sets_returns_zero(self):
        """Completely disjoint sets should yield 0.0."""
        result = compute_signal_overlap(["s1", "s2"], ["s3", "s4"])
        assert result == 0.0, f"Expected 0.0 for disjoint sets, got {result}"

    def test_partial_overlap_correct_ratio(self):
        """Partial overlap: |{s2,s3}|/|{s1,s2,s3,s4}| = 2/4 = 0.5."""
        result = compute_signal_overlap(["s1", "s2", "s3"], ["s2", "s3", "s4"])
        assert abs(result - 0.5) < 1e-9, f"Expected 0.5, got {result}"

    def test_symmetric(self):
        """Overlap must be symmetric: overlap(a, b) == overlap(b, a)."""
        a = ["s1", "s2"]
        b = ["s2", "s3", "s4"]
        result_ab = compute_signal_overlap(a, b)
        result_ba = compute_signal_overlap(b, a)
        assert result_ab == result_ba, (
            f"Symmetry violated: overlap(a,b)={result_ab} != overlap(b,a)={result_ba}"
        )

    def test_one_empty_returns_zero(self):
        """One empty, one non-empty should yield 0.0."""
        result = compute_signal_overlap([], ["s1"])
        assert result == 0.0, f"Expected 0.0 when one set is empty, got {result}"

    def test_result_bounded_zero_one(self):
        """Result should always be in [0.0, 1.0]."""
        result = compute_signal_overlap(["s1"], ["s1", "s2", "s3", "s4", "s5"])
        assert 0.0 <= result <= 1.0, f"Result {result} out of [0.0, 1.0] bounds"


class TestComputeAssessmentAgreement:
    """Tests for compute_assessment_agreement."""

    def test_no_shared_signals_returns_zero(self):
        """No shared signal IDs -> 0.0 agreement."""
        a = [make_assessment("s1", "ACCEPT", 0.8)]
        b = [make_assessment("s2", "ACCEPT", 0.8)]
        result = compute_assessment_agreement(a, b, 0.05)
        assert result == 0.0, f"Expected 0.0, got {result}"

    def test_full_agreement(self):
        """All shared signals agree on decision and familiarity within epsilon -> 1.0."""
        a = [
            make_assessment("s1", "ACCEPT", 0.80),
            make_assessment("s2", "ACCEPT", 0.60),
        ]
        b = [
            make_assessment("s1", "ACCEPT", 0.82),
            make_assessment("s2", "ACCEPT", 0.58),
        ]
        result = compute_assessment_agreement(a, b, 0.05)
        assert result == 1.0, f"Expected 1.0, got {result}"

    def test_decision_mismatch_returns_zero(self):
        """Different decisions on same signal -> 0.0 agreement for that pair."""
        a = [make_assessment("s1", "ACCEPT", 0.8)]
        b = [make_assessment("s1", "REJECT", 0.8)]
        result = compute_assessment_agreement(a, b, 0.05)
        assert result == 0.0, f"Expected 0.0, got {result}"

    def test_epsilon_boundary_exact(self):
        """Familiarity scores exactly epsilon apart should be considered agreeing."""
        a = [make_assessment("s1", "ACCEPT", 0.50)]
        b = [make_assessment("s1", "ACCEPT", 0.55)]
        result = compute_assessment_agreement(a, b, 0.05)
        assert result == 1.0, f"Expected 1.0 at epsilon boundary, got {result}"

    def test_epsilon_exceeded(self):
        """Familiarity scores beyond epsilon should disagree even with same decision."""
        a = [make_assessment("s1", "ACCEPT", 0.50)]
        b = [make_assessment("s1", "ACCEPT", 0.56)]
        result = compute_assessment_agreement(a, b, 0.05)
        assert result == 0.0, f"Expected 0.0 beyond epsilon, got {result}"

    def test_symmetric(self):
        """Agreement must be symmetric: agreement(a, b, eps) == agreement(b, a, eps)."""
        a = [
            make_assessment("s1", "ACCEPT", 0.80),
            make_assessment("s2", "REJECT", 0.30),
            make_assessment("s3", "ACCEPT", 0.60),
        ]
        b = [
            make_assessment("s1", "ACCEPT", 0.85),
            make_assessment("s2", "REJECT", 0.30),
        ]
        result_ab = compute_assessment_agreement(a, b, 0.05)
        result_ba = compute_assessment_agreement(b, a, 0.05)
        assert result_ab == result_ba, (
            f"Symmetry violated: {result_ab} != {result_ba}"
        )

    def test_duplicate_signal_raises_valueerror(self):
        """Assessment list with duplicate signal_id should raise ValueError."""
        a_dup = [
            make_assessment("s1", "ACCEPT", 0.8),
            make_assessment("s1", "REJECT", 0.5),
        ]
        b = [make_assessment("s1", "ACCEPT", 0.8)]
        with pytest.raises(ValueError) as exc:
            compute_assessment_agreement(a_dup, b, 0.05)
        assert "duplicate" in str(exc.value).lower() or "signal_id" in str(exc.value).lower(), (
            f"Expected duplicate signal error, got: {exc.value}"
        )

    def test_both_empty_returns_zero(self):
        """Both assessment lists empty -> 0.0."""
        result = compute_assessment_agreement([], [], 0.05)
        assert result == 0.0, f"Expected 0.0, got {result}"

class TestCheckMerges:

        assessments = [make_assessment(s, "ACCEPT", 0.8) for s in shared]
        ctx1 = make_context_snapshot(

        )

            neighbors=[make_neighbor("ctx-1"), make_neighbor("ctx-3")],
        )
        ctx3 = make_context_snapshot(
            context_id="ctx-3",
            signal_ids=["s99"],
            assessments=[make_assessment("s99", "REJECT", 0.1)],
            energy=5.0,
            neighbors=[make_neighbor("ctx-1"), make_neighbor("ctx-2")],
        )
        return [ctx1, ctx2, ctx3]

    def test_happy_path_returns_qualifying_pairs(self):
        """Only pairs meeting both thresholds appear in results."""
        snapshots = self._make_high_overlap_triple()
        config = make_merge_config(overlap_threshold=0.7, agreement_threshold=0.8)
        states = {"ctx-1": "STABLE", "ctx-2": "STABLE", "ctx-3": "STABLE"}
        result = check_merges(snapshots, config, states)
        for p in result:
            assert p.overlap_score >= config.overlap_threshold, (
                f"Proposal overlap {p.overlap_score} below threshold"
            )
            assert p.agreement_score >= config.agreement_threshold, (
                f"Proposal agreement {p.agreement_score} below threshold"
            )

    def test_skips_non_stable_contexts(self):
        """Contexts not in STABLE state should be skipped."""
        snapshots = self._make_high_overlap_triple()
        config = make_merge_config(overlap_threshold=0.5, agreement_threshold=0.5)
        states = {"ctx-1": "STABLE", "ctx-2": "MERGING", "ctx-3": "STABLE"}
        result = check_merges(snapshots, config, states)
        for p in result:
            assert p.source_context_id != "ctx-2" and p.target_context_id != "ctx-2", (
                f"Non-STABLE context 'ctx-2' appeared in proposal: {p}"
            )

    def test_no_duplicate_unordered_pairs(self):
        """Each unordered pair of contexts appears at most once."""
        snapshots = self._make_high_overlap_triple()
        config = make_merge_config(overlap_threshold=0.1, agreement_threshold=0.0)
        states = {"ctx-1": "STABLE", "ctx-2": "STABLE", "ctx-3": "STABLE"}
        result = check_merges(snapshots, config, states)
        pairs = []
        for p in result:
            pair = frozenset([p.source_context_id, p.target_context_id])
            pairs.append(pair)
        assert len(pairs) == len(set(pairs)), (
            f"Duplicate unordered pairs found: {pairs}"
        )

            make_lifecycle_proposal(kind="DECAY", affected_context_ids=["ctx-1"], priority=0),

            f"{len(result.rejected_proposals)} rejected proposals"
        )

    def test_partition_invariant(self):
        """accepted + rejected == total input count."""
        proposals = [
            make_lifecycle_proposal(kind="FORK", affected_context_ids=["ctx-1"], priority=2),
            make_lifecycle_proposal(kind="DECAY", affected_context_ids=["ctx-1"], priority=0),
            make_lifecycle_proposal(kind="DECAY", affected_context_ids=["ctx-2"], priority=0),
            make_lifecycle_proposal(
                kind="MERGE",
                affected_context_ids=["ctx-2", "ctx-3"],

                merge_proposal=make_merge_proposal("ctx-2", "ctx-3"),
            ),
            make_lifecycle_proposal(kind="FORK", affected_context_ids=["ctx-3"], priority=2),
        ]
        total = len(proposals)
        result = resolve_lifecycle_conflicts(proposals)
        assert len(result.accepted_proposals) + len(result.rejected_proposals) == total, (
            f"Partition invariant violated: {len(result.accepted_proposals)} + "
            f"{len(result.rejected_proposals)} != {total}"
        )

                merge_proposal=make_merge_proposal("ctx-3", "ctx-4"),

        ]
        result = resolve_lifecycle_conflicts(proposals)

        assert len(all_ids) == len(set(all_ids)), (

        )

class TestConfigSensitivity:
    """Tests for threshold and config boundary behavior."""

    def _make_pair_with_exact_overlap(self, overlap_ratio):
        """Build two contexts with a specific Jaccard overlap ratio.

        For overlap_ratio = n/(n + m), we create n shared signals and m unique signals.
        We use a simple case: total union size = 10, intersection = round(overlap_ratio * 10).
        """
        union_size = 10
        intersection_size = max(0, min(union_size, round(overlap_ratio * union_size)))
        shared = [f"s-shared-{i}" for i in range(intersection_size)]
        only_a = [f"s-a-{i}" for i in range(union_size - intersection_size)]
        # To make the union exactly 10, context B gets the shared + (union - intersection) unique
        only_b_count = union_size - intersection_size
        only_b = [f"s-b-{i}" for i in range(only_b_count)]

        assessments_shared = [make_assessment(s, "ACCEPT", 0.8) for s in shared]
        assessments_a = assessments_shared + [make_assessment(s, "ACCEPT", 0.8) for s in only_a]
        assessments_b = assessments_shared + [make_assessment(s, "ACCEPT", 0.8) for s in only_b]

        ctx_a = make_context_snapshot(
            context_id="ctx-a",
            signal_ids=shared + only_a,
            assessments=assessments_a,
            energy=5.0,
            neighbors=[make_neighbor("ctx-b")],
        )
        ctx_b = make_context_snapshot(
            context_id="ctx-b",
            signal_ids=shared + only_b,
            assessments=assessments_b,
            energy=10.0,
            neighbors=[make_neighbor("ctx-a")],
        )
        return ctx_a, ctx_b

    def test_overlap_just_below_threshold_returns_none(self):
        """Overlap just below threshold should not produce a proposal."""
        config = make_merge_config(overlap_threshold=0.7, agreement_threshold=0.0)
        # Create contexts with overlap ~0.6 (6/10)
        ctx_a, ctx_b = self._make_pair_with_exact_overlap(0.6)
        result = check_merge(ctx_a, ctx_b, config)
        assert result is None, f"Expected None for overlap below threshold, got proposal"

    def test_overlap_at_threshold_returns_proposal(self):
        """Overlap exactly at threshold should produce a proposal."""
        config = make_merge_config(overlap_threshold=0.7, agreement_threshold=0.0)
        # overlap = 7/10 = 0.7
        ctx_a, ctx_b = self._make_pair_with_exact_overlap(0.7)
        result = check_merge(ctx_a, ctx_b, config)
        # Due to rounding: this should be right at the threshold
        if result is not None:
            assert result.overlap_score >= config.overlap_threshold

    def test_redirect_ttl_propagates_to_result(self):
        """execute_merge should use the config's redirect_ttl_seconds."""
        shared = ["s1", "s2", "s3"]
        assessments = [make_assessment(s, "ACCEPT", 0.8) for s in shared]
        ctx_a = make_context_snapshot(
            context_id="ctx-src",
            signal_ids=shared,
            assessments=assessments,
            agent_ids=["a1"],
            energy=5.0,
            neighbors=[make_neighbor("ctx-tgt")],
        )
        ctx_b = make_context_snapshot(
            context_id="ctx-tgt",
            signal_ids=shared,
            assessments=assessments,
            agent_ids=["a2"],
            energy=10.0,
            neighbors=[make_neighbor("ctx-src")],
        )
        proposal = make_merge_proposal("ctx-src", "ctx-tgt")
        config = make_merge_config(redirect_ttl_seconds=600.0)
        result = execute_merge(ctx_a, ctx_b, proposal, config)
        assert result.redirect.ttl_seconds == 600.0, (
            f"Expected TTL 600.0, got {result.redirect.ttl_seconds}"
        )

    def test_merge_config_rejects_overlap_threshold_zero(self):
        """MergeConfig should reject overlap_threshold of 0.0 (must be > 0.0)."""
        with pytest.raises((ValueError, Exception)) as exc:
            make_merge_config(overlap_threshold=0.0)
        # The validator says "overlap_threshold must be in (0.0, 1.0]"

    def test_merge_config_rejects_negative_window(self):
        """MergeConfig should reject negative window_seconds."""
        with pytest.raises((ValueError, Exception)) as exc:
            make_merge_config(window_seconds=-1.0)

class TestInvariants:
    """Cross-cutting invariant tests derived from contract invariants."""

    def test_mutual_exclusion_via_guard(self):
        """A context in MERGING cannot also enter FORKING or DECAYING."""
        states = {"ctx-1": "MERGING"}
        assert check_lifecycle_guard("ctx-1", "FORKING", states) is False
        assert check_lifecycle_guard("ctx-1", "DECAYING", states) is False

    def test_mutual_exclusion_forking(self):
        """A context in FORKING cannot also enter MERGING or DECAYING."""
        states = {"ctx-1": "FORKING"}
        assert check_lifecycle_guard("ctx-1", "MERGING", states) is False
        assert check_lifecycle_guard("ctx-1", "DECAYING", states) is False

    def test_mutual_exclusion_decaying(self):
        """A context in DECAYING cannot also enter MERGING or FORKING."""
        states = {"ctx-1": "DECAYING"}
        assert check_lifecycle_guard("ctx-1", "MERGING", states) is False
        assert check_lifecycle_guard("ctx-1", "FORKING", states) is False

    def test_pure_functions_are_deterministic(self):
        """Pure functions called twice with same input should give same output."""
        signals = ["s1", "s2", "s3"]
        r1 = compute_signal_overlap(signals, ["s2", "s3", "s4"])
        r2 = compute_signal_overlap(signals, ["s2", "s3", "s4"])
        assert r1 == r2, "compute_signal_overlap is not deterministic"

        assessments_a = [make_assessment("s1", "ACCEPT", 0.8)]
        assessments_b = [make_assessment("s1", "ACCEPT", 0.82)]
        a1 = compute_assessment_agreement(assessments_a, assessments_b, 0.05)
        a2 = compute_assessment_agreement(assessments_a, assessments_b, 0.05)
        assert a1 == a2, "compute_assessment_agreement is not deterministic"

    def test_redirect_map_has_finite_ttl(self):
        """All redirect entries created by execute_merge must have positive finite TTL."""
        shared = ["s1", "s2"]
        assessments = [make_assessment(s, "ACCEPT", 0.8) for s in shared]
        ctx_a = make_context_snapshot(
            context_id="ctx-src",
            signal_ids=shared,
            assessments=assessments,
            energy=5.0,
            neighbors=[make_neighbor("ctx-tgt")],
        )
        ctx_b = make_context_snapshot(
            context_id="ctx-tgt",
            signal_ids=shared,
            assessments=assessments,
            energy=10.0,
            neighbors=[make_neighbor("ctx-src")],
        )
        proposal = make_merge_proposal("ctx-src", "ctx-tgt")
        config = make_merge_config(redirect_ttl_seconds=300.0)
        result = execute_merge(ctx_a, ctx_b, proposal, config)
        assert result.redirect.ttl_seconds > 0.0, (
            f"TTL must be positive, got {result.redirect.ttl_seconds}"
        )
        assert result.redirect.ttl_seconds < float("inf"), "TTL must be finite"
